label: A: 25, no symptoms, online ad
card_text: A 25-year-old with no symptoms and no family history sees an ad and orders a Cologuard. It comes back positive.
discussion: How many false positives are there per cancer found? What is their risk-equivalent age?

label: B: 28, father diagnosed at 50
card_text: A 28-year-old whose father was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at 50. Their clinic offers Cologuard.
discussion: When would guidelines start screening? Does the model's risk-equivalent age agree?

label: C: 24, MLH1 Lynch variant
card_text: A 24-year-old found through cascade testing to carry a pathogenic MLH1 variant asks whether a yearly stool test is enough.
discussion: Compare FIT with colonoscopy. How many cancers are missed per 10,000? Why do guidelines use colonoscopy?

label: D: 27, rectal bleeding + anemia
card_text: A 27-year-old with 3 months of rectal bleeding and iron-deficiency anemia. Their FIT is negative.
discussion: Is this screening or diagnosis? What is the chance of cancer after a NEGATIVE FIT? Is that low enough to stop?

label: E: 35, top-decile polygenic score
card_text: A 35-year-old gets a direct-to-consumer report putting them in the top 10% for polygenic CRC risk. They also drink heavily. They ask for the Shield blood test.
discussion: How much does the polygenic score move the risk-equivalent age compared with a family history?

label: F: 55, average risk, FIT
card_text: A 55-year-old at average risk chooses a yearly FIT for screening.
discussion: Compare with scenario A. Same kind of test: why is the positive predictive value so different?
